finding.title: Replace raw Colors.* literals with theme colors in content_browsing widgets
finding.why: Every other color reference in this batch routes through AppTheme.brand*/Theme.of(context).colorScheme.*; these three raw Colors.* literals won't repaint with a future theme/brand change, and since dart run custom_lint is currently broken (baselined separately), nothing catches new instances of this today.
finding.recommendation: Swap Colors.grey for theme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant (matching the sibling separator in breadcrumb_navigation.dart) and the two Colors.white for the equivalent theme token used elsewhere in text_display_screen.dart.
acceptance_criteria: once dart run custom_lint is repaired, no_color_literal_outside_theme reports zero hits in these 2 files

finding.title: Remove the false 'Bundled JSON removed' skip on ContentRepositoryImpl's acceptance suite in content_repository_test.dart
finding.rule: TQ-7 (honest skip/weaken reason) / TQ-8 (bug fix needs a real regression test)

evidence.quote: skip: 'Bundled JSON removed — content now fetched from cloud storage',
skip: 'Bundled JSON removed — content now fetched from cloud storage',
/// Retained for potential future use (content updates, text downloads).

finding.why: I removed both `skip:` parameters and ran `flutter test` against the real bundled assets: 8 of 9 tests in the first group passed immediately, proving bundled JSON was never removed — 16 curricula still ship under assets/content/hierarchy/*.json (declared in pubspec.yaml:202), and ContentRepositoryImpl (the asset-JSON reader) is the live implementation behind contentRepositoryProvider; CloudContentService is explicitly commented 'Retained for potential future use', i.e. not wired into content loading at all. The 9th test — searching 'Berakhot' — failed with an empty result: ContentRepositoryImpl.search() indexes CurriculumLabelRenderer's Ashkenazi-transliterated leaf names ('Berakhos'), not the raw displayNameEn ('Berakhot') the real asset data and the test both use, so a user who types the un-transliterated spelling gets zero search results. Instead of fixing the index or correcting the query, someone silenced the entire 11-test suite (both the acceptance and performance groups) with an unrelated, false excuse — leaving the real-asset load/parse/config/filter path for all 16 curricula (the mechanism every content-browsing screen ultimately depends on) without automated regression coverage, and hiding a real search-matching gap behind a skip reason that reads as 'not applicable' rather than 'known failure'.
finding.recommendation: Remove both `skip:` parameters. Either fix ContentRepositoryImpl.search to also match the raw/un-rendered displayNameEn (so both transliteration spellings resolve), or, if only the rendered form should ever be searchable, change the test's query to the Ashkenazi-rendered spelling with a one-line comment explaining why the raw spelling intentionally doesn't match. Re-run the full file to confirm all 11 tests pass against real assets.
acceptance_criteria: `flutter test test/features/content_browsing/data/repositories/content_repository_test.dart` passes end-to-end with no `skip:` on either group.
The 'search returns items matching Hebrew or English query' test passes against real bundled assets (index fixed, or query corrected with a stated reason).

finding.title: Make pp18_content_search_clear_button_test.dart render the real ContentSearchScreen instead of a hand-rolled TextField clone
finding.rule: TQ-8 (tautological test — doesn't exercise the code it claims to protect)

evidence.quote: /// Helper: builds a minimal TextField that mirrors the ContentSearchScreen

finding.why: This file's docstring says it is the regression test for PP-18 ('No clear (X) affordance in the content-search field') and claims to verify ContentSearchScreen's `InputDecoration.suffixIcon` is wired. It never imports content_search_screen.dart — its own comment admits `buildSearchField()` only 'mirrors' (re-implements by hand) the real screen's decoration logic. The real screen still has the suffixIcon wiring today (content_search_screen.dart:128-133), but I grepped every test in the repo that renders `ContentSearchScreen(` for real — content_search_screen_test.dart (this batch) and content_tile_search_providers_test.dart (outside it) — and neither checks `Icons.clear` or `suffixIcon`. So if a future edit to the real screen breaks or removes the clear button, every test in the repo, including the one named specifically for that bug, stays green.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite the test to pumpWidget the real ContentSearchScreen (reusing the provider overrides from content_search_screen_test.dart), enterText into the real search field, and assert the real Icons.clear IconButton appears/clears/disappears. Delete the hand-rolled buildSearchField helper.
acceptance_criteria: Test imports and pumps ContentSearchScreen; temporarily deleting the suffixIcon block in content_search_screen.dart makes this test fail.

finding.title: Move TextContent/TextSegment out of text_cache_repository.dart (data layer) into domain/entities/ so presentation and its tests stop importing the data layer
finding.rule: Presentation→data import ban [P]; naming/placement (domain models belong in domain/); Evans lens (bounded-context leak)
finding.why: TextContent/TextSegment are plain immutable data holders — exactly what domain/entities/ is for (that directory exists, scaffolded with a lone .gitkeep, but was never populated) — yet they are defined at the top of text_cache_repository.dart, the DATA-layer repository implementation. That forces text_display_screen.dart (presentation, and a churn HOTSPOT at 1028 lines) to import the data layer just to type its own widget fields (_TextContentView.textContent, _NumberedSegmentColumn.segments). It then forces every test that builds fixture content — 3 of this batch's files (text_display_screen_test.dart, _l1_test.dart, _deep_l1_test.dart) — to do the same, so the test suite faithfully pins the wrong layering instead of catching it. Concrete cost: a presentation test can't get a TextContent value without also pulling in TextCacheRepository's own Drift-DAO-typed constructor surface (the seam Feathers-style testability depends on is gone); a different feature that wanted to render cached text would have to import a repository class to get the model type; and this is a same-feature leak, so it isn't caught by make audit's Rule 1/2 greps (which are scoped to cross-feature imports).
finding.recommendation: Create lib/features/content_browsing/domain/entities/text_content.dart holding TextContent/TextSegment (mechanical move, no behavior change). Update text_cache_repository.dart and text_display_screen.dart (+ its tests) to import the new domain file instead of the repository file.
acceptance_criteria: text_display_screen_l1_test.dart, _deep_l1_test.dart, and text_display_screen_test.dart import domain/entities/text_content.dart, not data/repositories/text_cache_repository.dart, and still pass.

finding.title: Replace the 'accepts any exception' navigation assertion in hierarchy_navigation_test.dart and curriculum_list_screen_test.dart with real router verification
finding.rule: TQ-8 (assertion weaker than what the source can do wrong)
finding.why: Both tests tap a curriculum row and assert only that `tester.takeException()` is non-null — that passes for any exception at all, including an unrelated build error introduced by a future regression, not specifically the intended 'no AutoRouter in the test tree' push failure. hierarchy_navigation_test.dart also pre-builds elaborate filterByLevel mocks for three deeper drill levels (Berachos, Perek 1, Mishna 1) that are never exercised because the test ends at the very first tap — dead setup code that makes the test look far more thorough than it is. This same batch already contains the fix pattern in text_display_screen_l1_test.dart and r2_content_hierarchy_nav_test.dart: inject a mocktail `_MockStackRouter` via `StackRouterScope` and `verify()` the specific push/replace call.
finding.recommendation: Swap the AutoRouter-less MaterialApp harness for the StackRouterScope + _MockStackRouter pattern already used elsewhere in this batch, and verify() the specific route pushed. Delete or actually use the now-provably-dead multi-level filterByLevel mock setup in hierarchy_navigation_test.dart's first test.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests assert a specific route via verify(() => router.push(any(that: isA<ContentHierarchyRoute>()))) or equivalent, not `exception, isNotNull`.
